messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm about to flip the LB healthcheck wiring for inference-gateway svc to target IPs instead of instances to reduce the intermittent 502s we've seen on NLB. Need a quick QA + any caveats before I roll.

sam: Do we know if externalTrafficPolicy needs to be Local for this to work? I remember source IP preservation affects healthchecks sometimes.

alex_m: Also what about nodePort vs clusterIP? Changing targetType might change how probes hit endpoints.

maya: Good q. Current plan: keep externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster. We only change the annotation that tells the AWS LB controller to use targetType=ip. That should make healthchecks hit Pod IPs directly.

maya: Current k8s svc snippet in cluster:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "instance"   # currently
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8080
```

maya: I'll change the annotation to "ip" and update Terraform so the controller creates the NLB target groups with targetType=ip.

sam: If we switch to ip, healthchecks will be TCP by default, right? We should keep the probe path/check consistent with what our app exposes (http /healthz). Otherwise TG might mark targets unhealthy.

maya: Right — AWS TG for ip targets still supports HTTP/HTTPS healthchecks. We're setting health check to HTTP /live (app endpoint).

infra-bot: Reminder: changing targetType may require draining existing targets and the change could briefly drop connections while TGs re-register. Planned change window recommended.

lucy: @maya can you post the terraform diff you'll apply? Want to run plan locally quickly.

maya: Terraform change is tiny, adding annotation via the k8s_service resource and a comment in infra module. Snippet: 

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference_gateway" {
  metadata {
    name = "inference-gateway"
    annotations = {
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type" = "ip"
    }
  }
  spec { ... }
}
```

maya: Also adding a post-change note to run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` to verify targets are healthy.

sam: Sounds good. One more: does our ASG / instance security group still allow healthcheck from TG IPs? For ip targets, TGs will hit pod IPs on nodeENIs — security groups should allow node <-> pod traffic (we do), but double-checking for any hostNetwork pods.

alex_m: For rollout: can we do a canary by updating a single k8s svc in staging first, then prod RG next?

maya: Plan: staging apply now, monitor 5–10 mins, then prod during 30-min window. Rolling change so not all TGs replaced at once.

ops_oncall: I'll be on standby for the prod change window. Ping me before apply. Also note: if anything breaks, set annotation back to instance and reapply.

sam: +1. Also please add a note in the PR describing the npm/ingress change and link to the controller docs for targetType.

maya: Will do. Creating PR now, will include test plan and rollback steps. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops_oncall: FYI I ran a quick grep — ingress controller version we run supports targetType=ip since v1.4.0, so we're good.

maya: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/infrastructure/pull/412 — applying to staging in ~5m.

lucy: Reviewing PR now. Quick nit: add terraform state note for any manual TG cleanup if the controller doesn't reconcile cleanly.

maya: Added note. Will post results after staging apply.

(5m later)
maya: Staging apply done, healthchecks healthy, no 502s observed in the small spike we tested. Proceeding to prod at 21:30 UTC.

alex_m: Thanks, appreciate the runbook in PR.

ops_oncall: I'm watching.

maya: Prod apply done, brief spike but TGs converged, confirmed /live returns 200 for all targets. Rolling back not needed. Closing ticket. :tada:
